subject: test for variance inflation factors or not?

messages.author: 1cb68adbec0995e8
messages.subject: test for variance inflation factors or not?
parts:
Hello,

    I am doing a procD.pgls with shape against multiple categorical environmental factors and I will be looking not only at the main effects but interactions of those factors as well. I was planning on doing a vif from package 'car' to ensure that none of my factors are too highly collinear, but I noticed that the procD.pgls gave a warning that may indicate it's already be doing what the vif has done? Here's the message I got:

Warning: Because variables in the linear model are redundant,
the linear model design has been truncated (via QR decomposition).
Original X columns: 144
Final X columns (rank): 38
Check coefficients or degrees of freedom in ANOVA to see changes.

Thanks for your time!

Jessica

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] test for variance inflation factors or not?
parts:
Jessica,

That does not mean the same thing.  The QR decomposition warning is because one has a model design matrix, X, that has rank lower than the number of columns in X.  This is caused by the same variable more than once in the matrix, which most frequently occurs because of vectors of 0s.  The cause of vectors of 0s is most often missing interactions.  For example, if one has populations A, B, and C nested in species 1 and D and E in species 2, the species1:D, species1:E, species2:A, species2:B, and species2:C terms in the model design - columns in the design matrix - are all vectors of 0s.  These are removed via QR decomposition and the warning message is just to let you know it happened.  These columns of 0s will not be counted toward degrees of freedom and removing them will help to make sure there are no computation errors in calculating linear model coefficients.

If this is what you meant by collinear factors, then yes, it was adjusted naturally by the analysis.

Cheers!
Mike
